audit.report: The database recovery negotiation for the checkout workload escalated after three rounds without agreement. The root blocker was a batch_replayable_inventory worker (pid 330157) idle in transaction for 4.1 seconds with a 'SELECT 1' last statement, blocking 12 sessions and reducing checkout success to 53%. The Database Guardian repeatedly proposed waiting, citing the blocker's short transaction time and no protected settlements in flight. The Continuity Guardian rejected each proposal because the business federation outage made workload registry, change calendar, and biz.impact data unavailable, preventing quantification of the cost of waiting versus terminating. No action was executed; the incident was escalated to on-call after 139 seconds.
audit.root_cause: Business federation outage prevented retrieval of workload replayability, change calendar, and impact data required to evaluate the tradeoff of waiting versus terminating the batch_replayable_inventory blocker.
lessons: Cache workload registry replayability and interrupt policy for batch_replayable_inventory locally so the Database Guardian can propose with evidence during federation outages.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian wasted rounds 2 and 3 by re-proposing wait with identical evidence after the Continuity Guardian explicitly required biz.tradeoff data that was known unavailable since round 1. The Continuity Guardian correctly held the invariant (I7) but did not offer a fallback decision path when federation data was missing.
follow_ups: Implement local cache for workload registry data (replayability, interrupt policy) for batch_replayable_inventory and other critical workloads.
